Envelope and request helpers:
  assert_envelope(env: dict, *, as_gap: bool = False) -> None   # wraps dms_executor.envelope.assert_envelope_valid (E1-E9). Default raises ControlFailed (precondition). as_gap=True re-raises the plain AssertionError for when "envelope malformed" IS the gap.

A gap test is only as good as its control: gate_gap catches AssertionError, so a plain `assert` that fails inside the HARNESS or product code on a different cause still XFAILs. Put preconditions behind control/require_envelope/assert_envelope and keep exactly one plain assert for the gap itself.
The gate_gap mark uses kwargs (row=, gate=, ticket=, gap_id=), so a report script must read mark.kwargs, not mark.args.

1. followup-no-grant-recheck is two tests because the primary repro and the secondary are independent mechanisms. The no-Space test encodes the dms#303 FOLLOWUP-CONTRACT-01 item 3 expectation (abstain no_space) as quoted in gaps.json and docs/subagents_findings/gate-matrix.md; I could not read the ruling itself. Note the pack lane deliberately serves no-space_id asks under the 'Company (default ACL)' scope (demo_grants.company_default_tables), so the no_space expectation on the follow-up comes from the ruling and the bronze-lane precedent, not from the pack lane. The revoked-grant test does not depend on the ruling: the upload is re-homed from FINANCE to WAREHOUSE_OPS in the ingest registry (same state test_bronze_grant_01's cross-Space case seeds), a fresh session's bronze ask is refused ungranted_table, yet the old session's follow-up still averages the figures. 2. followup-no-submit: the gate assertion accepts either an abstain or (2 SQL submits, 2 ledger appends, audit_id equal to the fake's ledger entry id), so it does not prescribe the fix shape. 3. followup-unit-relabelled-rm: the gap assertion is 'abstained OR no RM in text and no *myr* value label'.
